artist_statement.text:
Sina Beizavi in Brazil

7 months have passed since queer artist Sina Beizavinejad escaped from Iran, where the regime made him live in constant fear for his life due to his sexuality, artistic expression and his renunciation of islam. His situation was aggravated by USA sanctions against Iranian citizens, which further limited his expression, even through web3 systems. His migration to Brazil was enabled by Casa NUA's embrace of the 6529 network, and the network's support of Casa NUA in return.

In the photograph, Sina (@[AWD]) rests from his work week at Casa NUA on a Sunday afternoon, wearing only his Havaianas in brazilian colors – his welcome gift from Hugo Faz – while nonchalantly holding his Iranian passport, now finally free to live fully in his own skin.

Digital photograph, directed, shot and color graded by Hugo Faz. 

I, Hugo Faz, hereby confirm that I hold full rights over the submitted work and the person depicted has also given formal written consent for this work to be released under CC0, relinquishing all copyright and related rights, and permanently accessioned as part of the 6529 Network Museum collection. Written consent documentation is available and can be provided upon request.

Shot on July 5th, 2026, in Casa NUA, São Paulo, Brazil, and submitted to Keys and gates on the same date.
